key_insight: AI-generated handoffs were rated similarly to clinician handoffs overall, with stronger organization and completeness but weaker conciseness and accuracy.
clinical_relevance: Generative AI could reduce handoff documentation burden in hospital medicine, but its different error pattern means safety checks are still needed before routine use.
method: Retrospective comparison of AI-generated vs clinician-authored end-of-rotation handoffs.
AI handoffs were produced from clinical notes using a large language model.
A structured review scored quality and safety domains across handoffs.
evidence_signal: Overall quality scores were similar (3.7 vs 3.5), with equal error rates (0.3 per handoff) but different error types between groups.
watch_item: AI handoffs included inaccuracies and rare hallucinations, so prospective testing in real clinical workflows is important before implementation.
paper_title: Quality and Safety profiles of AI-Generated vs Clinician-Generated Handoffs in Hospital Medicine
